        <div style="font-family: Open Sans, sans-serif; position: relative; overflow: hidden;">
        <p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" class="size-full wp-image-281273 img-responsive alignright" src="https://ieeecs-media.computer.org/wp-media/2022/06/08164630/Programing-Languages-Timeline.jpg" alt="A history of programming languages" width="250" height="250" srcset="https://ieeecs-media.computer.org/wp-media/2022/06/08164630/Programing-Languages-Timeline.jpg 250w, https://ieeecs-media.computer.org/wp-media/2022/06/08164630/Programing-Languages-Timeline-150x150.jpg 150w, https://ieeecs-media.computer.org/wp-media/2022/06/08164630/Programing-Languages-Timeline-100x100.jpg 100w" sizes="(max-width: 250px) 100vw, 250px" />Coding and programming languages are the building blocks of our modern digital world. But although the most significant developments in this field have happened within living memory, the history of coding and the timeline of programming languages is longer than you might think.</p>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">It starts with surprising and remarkable people, long before the birth of other types of commonplace technology like cars and telephones. It even predates modern medical treatments we take for granted, such as insulin and antibiotics. In fact, coding dates back to the 1840s.</p>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">Let’s take a closer look at the history of coding and the timeline of programming languages.</p>
<p> </p>
<hr style="width: 100%;" />
<p> </p>
<p style="text-align: center; color: #ff6600;"><a href="https://www.computer.org/resources/newsletters/computing-edge?source=technews"><strong>Want More Tech News? Subscribe to <i>ComputingEdge</i> Newsletter Today!</strong></a></p>
<p> </p>
<hr style="width: 100%;" />
<p> </p>
<h2 style="color: #002855; font-size: 24px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 29px;">Origins</h2>
<hr style="text-align: left; width: 30%; height: 3px; color: #ffa300; background-color: #ffa300; border: none;" />
<h3 style="color: #002855; font-size: 20px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px;">1843 Ada Lovelace</h3>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;"><img decoding="async" class="size-medium wp-image-281308 img-responsive alignleft" src="https://ieeecs-media.computer.org/wp-media/2022/06/08175353/Timeline-of-Programming-Languages-2-200x300.png" alt="Ada Lovelace" width="200" height="300" srcset="https://ieeecs-media.computer.org/wp-media/2022/06/08175353/Timeline-of-Programming-Languages-2-200x300.png 200w, https://ieeecs-media.computer.org/wp-media/2022/06/08175353/Timeline-of-Programming-Languages-2.png 341w" sizes="(max-width: 200px) 100vw, 200px" />Ada Lovelace was a British aristocrat; unusually for a woman of her time, she was educated in mathematics and science. However, her contribution to the development of coding and computer languages is not that she invented a device that was the breakthrough of Charles Babbage in the 1820s with his Difference Machine. Instead, Lovelace created the very first machine algorithm in 1843.</p>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">She realized that Babbage’s machine could do more than just calculate; it could be used as a general-purpose machine. Lovelace made the leap that numbers could represent other things, and the idea of programming languages was born. Lovelace’s groundbreaking work was the first step in being able to <a href="https://www.computer.org/csdl/magazine/co/2012/02/mco2012020007/13rRUy08MzA" target="_blank" rel="noopener">design a language</a> capable of giving computers instructions.</p>
<p> </p>
<h2 style="color: #002855; font-size: 24px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 29px;">The 20th Century</h2>
<p> </p>
<h3 style="color: #002855; font-size: 20px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px;">1936 Alan Turing</h3>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">Today, Alan Turing is famous for his work on cracking Nazi Germany’s Enigma code machine in 1939. But in 1936, Turing published a paper regarded as the founding piece on computer science. Turing came up with the concept of a universal machine. A machine that could follow instructions. He eventually turned this groundbreaking idea into a plan for a computer powered by electricity that could run programs.</p>
<p> </p>
<h3 style="color: #002855; font-size: 20px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px;">1940s Konrad Zuse</h3>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">Konrad Zuse created what is considered the first programming language for computers in the early 1940s. It was called Plankalkul, and it could store codes, enabling engineers to carry out routine, repetitive tasks far more efficiently and quickly.</p>
<p> </p>
<h3 style="color: #002855; font-size: 20px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px;">1949 Assembly Language and Shortcode</h3>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">The next big development was Assembly language, a computer programming language that simplified the instructions to make a computer function. Also, in 1949 came Shortcode, used by</p>
<p><img decoding="async" class="size-medium wp-image-281309 img-responsive alignright" src="https://ieeecs-media.computer.org/wp-media/2022/06/08175442/Timeline-of-Programming-Languages-3-300x171.png" alt="Assembly Language and Shortcode" width="300" height="171" srcset="https://ieeecs-media.computer.org/wp-media/2022/06/08175442/Timeline-of-Programming-Languages-3-300x171.png 300w, https://ieeecs-media.computer.org/wp-media/2022/06/08175442/Timeline-of-Programming-Languages-3.png 512w" sizes="(max-width: 300px) 100vw, 300px" /></p>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;"> William Schmitt with the BINAC and UNIVAC computers.</p>
<h3 style="color: #002855; font-size: 20px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px;">1952 Autocode</h3>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">In 1952 Autocode was developed for the Mark 1 computer at the University of Manchester. It was the first language that could be translated into machine code.</p>
<p> </p>
<h3 style="color: #002855; font-size: 20px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px;">1957 Fortran</h3>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">John Backus created FORmula TRANslation or FORTRAN back in 1957. Incredibly, this programming language from the 1950s is still used today in supercomputers and scientific and mathematical computations.</p>
<p> </p>
<h3 style="color: #002855; font-size: 20px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px;">1958 ALGOL and LISP</h3>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">An algorithmic language created by American and European scientists, ALGOL became the point of origin for world-renowned programming languages such as Pascal, Java, C, and C++.</p>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">In the same year, John McCarthy invented the List processor or LISP. Intended for AI, companies like Boeing and Genworks are still using it.</p>
<p> </p>
<h3 style="color: #002855; font-size: 20px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px;">1959 COBOL</h3>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">COBOL was developed by a team led by Dr. Grace Murray Hopper; COBOL stands for Common Business Oriented Language. It was designed for credit card transaction processors, traffic signals, and phone calls, and today is used in banking and gaming. Today’s <a href="https://www.ringcentral.co.uk/office/features/virtual-pbx/overview.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">virtual PBX system</a> and other modern solutions to communication rest on the shoulders of programming languages like COBOL.</p>
<p> </p>
<h3 style="color: #002855; font-size: 20px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px;">1964 BASIC</h3>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">Students developed BASIC at Dartmouth College. It stands for Beginners All-Purpose Symbolic Instruction Code. BASIC was then further developed and marketed as a product by Bill Gates.</p>
<p> </p>
<h3 style="color: #002855; font-size: 20px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px;">1970 PASCAL</h3>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">Niklaus Wirth developed this programming language and named it after Blaise Pascal, the French mathematician. So easy to learn, it was used by Apple early on in its history.</p>
<p> </p>
<h3 style="color: #002855; font-size: 20px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px;">1972 Smalltalk, C, and SQL</h3>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">Alan Kay, Adele Goldberg, and Dan Ingalls developed Smalltalk at the Xerox Palo Alto Research Centre. It was designed to modify code. Its principles are present in today’s Java, Python, and Ruby and are used by companies like CrowdStrike and Logitech.</p>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">C was also developed in 1972 by Dennis Ritchie at the Bell Telephone Laboratories. It was designed to be used with the Unix operating system. Based on its forerunner B, languages like C#, Java, JavaScript, Perl, PHP, and Python are all derived from C.</p>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">In what could be called a vintage year for coding and programming languages, Raymond Boyce and Donald Chamberlain developed SQL (Structured Query Language) the same year. It was first called SEQUEL, and it was used for viewing and altering information in databases.</p>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">These three languages represent a significant leap forward in programming, which has impacted some of the largest tech companies in existence today. Our whole way of using the digital world, from social media to how a business’s <a href="https://affise.com/blog/referral-program-examples-to-fuel-your-customer-acquisition/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">lead referral program</a> functions, owes a debt to these developments.</p>
<p> </p>
<h3 style="color: #002855; font-size: 20px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px;">1980s ADA</h3>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="size-medium wp-image-281311 img-responsive alignright" src="https://ieeecs-media.computer.org/wp-media/2022/06/08175551/Timeline-of-Programming-Languages-4-300x196.png" alt="1980s ADA" width="300" height="196" srcset="https://ieeecs-media.computer.org/wp-media/2022/06/08175551/Timeline-of-Programming-Languages-4-300x196.png 300w, https://ieeecs-media.computer.org/wp-media/2022/06/08175551/Timeline-of-Programming-Languages-4.png 512w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 300px) 100vw, 300px" />Named after Ada Lovelace, the computing pioneer, ADA was designed by Jean Ichbiah’s team at CUU Honeywell Bull. Ada is a high-level programming language, extended from other popular programming languages such as Pascal. ADA is used for air-traffic control in various European countries and space programs.</p>
<p> </p>
<h3 style="color: #002855; font-size: 20px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px;">1983 C++, Objective C</h3>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">Bjarne Stroustrup modified the C language at Bell Labs. The result was C++, which had some augmentations such as classes, templates, and virtual functions. C++ is now used in MS Office, Adobe Photoshop, and various types of high-performance software.</p>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">Brad Cox and Tom Love then developed Objective-C, the programming language used for Apple’s operating systems.</p>
<p> </p>
<h3 style="color: #002855; font-size: 20px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px;">1987 Perl</h3>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">Larry Wall developed PERL as a general-purpose, high-level language. He designed it for text editing, but today its primary use is in database applications, <a href="https://www.computer.org/csdl/proceedings-article/icde/2019/747400b980/1aDSRSNEWQM" target="_blank" rel="noopener">data processing</a>, graphic programming, and system administration.</p>
<p> </p>
<h3 style="color: #002855; font-size: 20px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px;">1990 Haskell</h3>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">Named after the American mathematician Haskell Brooks Curry. Haskell is a primarily mathematical programming language. Used in various industries that need to make complicated calculations, crunch numbers, and keep records.</p>
<p> </p>
<h3 style="color: #002855; font-size: 20px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px;">1991 Python and Visual Basic</h3>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">The iconic British comedy act Monty Python inspired Python’s name. Guido Van Rossum developed this general-purpose, high-level language. Today Python is one of the most popular programming languages worldwide. Giants like Google and Spotify use it.</p>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">Visual Basic allows a user to drag and drop sections of code via a user interface (GUI). Parts of Visual Basic are used in applications like Word and Excel.</p>
<p> </p>
<h3 style="color: #002855; font-size: 20px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px;">1993 Ruby</h3>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">Yukihiro Matsumoto created Ruby as a high-level programming language. Used for web applications development, today it’s used by Groupon.</p>
<p> </p>
<h3 style="color: #002855; font-size: 20px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px;">1995 Java, JavaScript, PHP</h3>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">Created by James Gosling in 1995, Java is one of the world’s most famous and popular programming languages. It’s a general-purpose, high-level language used in cell phones and parking machines.</p>
<p><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="size-medium wp-image-281312 img-responsive alignright" src="https://ieeecs-media.computer.org/wp-media/2022/06/08175618/Timeline-of-Programming-Languages-5-300x141.png" alt="Modern Java" width="300" height="141" srcset="https://ieeecs-media.computer.org/wp-media/2022/06/08175618/Timeline-of-Programming-Languages-5-300x141.png 300w, https://ieeecs-media.computer.org/wp-media/2022/06/08175618/Timeline-of-Programming-Languages-5.png 512w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 300px) 100vw, 300px" /></p>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">JavaScript was created by Brendan Eich. Used for web development, PDF documents, and desktop widgets, it’s on almost every major website. Some famous examples are Adobe, Gmail, and Mozilla Firefox.</p>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">PHP was known as ‘Personal Home Page’ but now stands for ‘Hypertext Preprocessor.’ It was developed by Rasmus Lerdorf. It’s used for building and maintaining web pages and server-side development. Huge companies like Facebook, Wikipedia, and WordPress use PHP.</p>
<p> </p>
<h2 style="color: #002855; font-size: 24px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 29px;">The 21st Century</h2>
<hr style="text-align: left; width: 30%; height: 3px; color: #ffa300; background-color: #ffa300; border: none;" />
<p> </p>
<h3 style="color: #002855; font-size: 20px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px;">2000 C#</h3>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">Microsoft developed C# in an attempt to combine elements of Visual Basic and C. It’s now used in all the company’s products.</p>
<p> </p>
<h3 style="color: #002855; font-size: 20px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px;">2003 Scala and Groovy</h3>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">In 2003 Martin Odersky created Scala. Its ability to work with Java gives it an advantage over Android development. Scala is used by social media and entertainment giants like Twitter, Linkedin, Twitter, and Netflix.</p>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">Groovy is an easy-to-learn language developed by James Strachan and Bob McWhirter. Starbucks, Craftbase, and Transferwise all use Groovy.</p>
<p> </p>
<h3 style="color: #002855; font-size: 20px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px;">2009 Go (Google)</h3>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">Large software systems face various challenges, and Google developed Go to resolve them.</p>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">Go is popular with big tech companies, such as Uber, Dropbox, and of course, Google. If you need to find out <a href="https://www.ringcentral.co.uk/gb/en/blog/definitions/vishing-voice-or-voip-phishing/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">what is vishing</a>? In part, you can thank Go for finding the answer.</p>
<p> </p>
<h3 style="color: #002855; font-size: 20px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 24px;">2014 Swift</h3>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">Apple developed Swift to replace C, C++, and Objective-C. The idea was that Swift would be easier and more versatile than these languages. Swift can be used for cloud applications, mobile, and desktop. Language platform Duolingo used it recently to launch a new app. Making apps that customers love using isn’t easy; these days, many companies use a <a href="https://www.globalapptesting.com/blog/how-to-build-a-mobile-app-that-customers-love" target="_blank" rel="noopener">mobile app flowchart</a>.</p>
<p>Image Source</p>
<h2 style="color: #002855; font-size: 24px; font-family: Montserrat; font-weight: 500; line-height: 29px;">Today and Tomorrow</h2>
<hr style="text-align: left; width: 30%; height: 3px; color: #ffa300; background-color: #ffa300; border: none;" />
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">Since the early days of 19th-century pioneers and 20th-century groundbreakers, the world of computing has expanded into cloud computing, a dizzying array of apps, new technology, and devices.</p>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">Some programming languages like COBOL and Fortran are still used today, while others have been through various incarnations or fallen out of use.</p>
<p style="color: #454545; font-size: 18px; font-family: Open Sans; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.7em;">Coding and computer languages will continue to develop and evolve, but just as Ada Lovelace probably couldn’t have imagined precisely what her ideas would mean for the centuries to come, who can say exactly what the next 180 years will hold.</p>
<p> </p>
